findings.claim: Skilled rehab therapy after a qualifying hospital stay is the covered SNF level of care.
findings.quote: requires skilled nursing services or skilled rehabilitation services
findings.case_fact: D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness.

findings.claim: Therapy followed an inpatient hospital stay for CHF.
findings.quote: the services are rendered for a condition for which the patient received inpatient hospital services
findings.case_fact: D.E. had a prior hospital stay for a diagnosis of congestive heart failure from August 23, 2009, to August 26, 2009.

findings.claim: Daily need is not settled by the facts (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: The patient requires these skilled services on a daily basis
findings.case_fact: the services were initiated on August 28, 2009, with treatment diagnoses of muscle weakness and lack of coordination.

findings.claim: Skilled observation and assessment is a covered skilled nursing service.
findings.quote: Observation and assessment are skilled services when the likelihood of change in a patient
findings.case_fact: On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate.

findings.claim: Fluctuating vital signs may justify skilled observation.
findings.quote: Such signs and symptoms as abnormal/fluctuating vital signs, weight changes, edema, symptoms of drug toxicity
findings.case_fact: The nursing staff was instructed to administer these medications based on fluctuating blood pressure readings

findings.claim: Nurse observation and assessment with potential treatment change is a covered skilled service.
findings.quote: Observation and assessment of the patient's condition by a nurse are reasonable and necessary skilled services
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary’s insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period.

findings.claim: Skilled care can continue for stable patients; diagnosis alone is not decisive.
findings.quote: Skilled care may, depending on the unique condition of the patient, continue to be necessary for patients whose condition is stable.
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary tested blood sugar levels on her own.

findings.claim: Skilled observation after hospital discharge to SNF is a covered skilled service.
findings.quote: Observation and assessment are skilled services when the likelihood of change in a patient
findings.case_fact: a physician indicated that the beneficiary required skilled nursing for one week to monitor for signs of fever, chills, clots

findings.claim: Abnormal lab values may justify skilled observation.
findings.quote: abnormal/fluctuating lab values
findings.case_fact: Laboratory results were abnormal.

findings.claim: PT is a skilled rehab service type, but link to qualifying hospital condition and SNF stay is unsettled.
findings.quote: the services are rendered for a condition for which the patient received inpatient hospital services
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s medical history was significant for a total right knee replacement (November 3, 2008)

findings.claim: Whether PT met the active written treatment plan and skilled-need conditions is not settled (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: The services must be directly and specifically related to an active written treatment plan
findings.case_fact: The appellant asserts that the beneficiary made steady progress throughout physical therapy

findings.claim: PT is a qualifying home health service type.
findings.quote: Be in need of skilled nursing care on an intermittent basis or physical therapy or speech-language pathology
findings.case_fact: these physical therapy services were provided in relation to the installation of a new stair lift mechanism

findings.claim: Confinement to the home is not stated in the facts (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: Be confined to the home
findings.case_fact: difficulty navigating stairs in his home due to fatigue, pain and abnormality of gait

findings.claim: Fistula care is within covered skilled wound care.
findings.quote: Care of wounds, (including, but not limited to, ulcers, burns, pressure sores, open surgical sites, fistulas, tube sites
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site.

findings.claim: Ostomy care reinforcement is skilled teaching covered under home health.
findings.quote: Teaching care for a recent ostomy or where reinforcement of ostomy care is needed
findings.case_fact: His bowel and bladder functions are maintained by colostomy and urostomy.

findings.claim: Part-time or intermittent aide and skilled nursing are covered types, but patient eligibility facts are absent.
findings.quote: Medicare covers either part-time or intermittent home health aide services or skilled nursing services
findings.case_fact: coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis

findings.claim: Patient must meet every section 30 criterion; none are shown in the facts (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: A patient must meet each of the criteria specified in this section.
findings.case_fact: whether Medicare covered at least 28 hours and up to 35 hours of the home health services furnished to the beneficiary

findings.claim: IRF is a covered benefit type only if regulatory requirements are met; facts give no clinical detail.
findings.quote: if the patient meets all of the requirements outlined in 42 CFR § 412.622(a)(3), (4), and (5)
findings.case_fact: This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004.

findings.claim: Beneficiary moved from acute hospital to IRF after knee replacement.
findings.quote: A patient who has not yet completed the full course of treatment in the referring hospital is expected to remain
findings.case_fact: Two days later, on July 17, 2003, the beneficiary was transferred and admitted to the appellant’s IRF where she received treatment

findings.claim: Ability to actively participate in intensive therapy is unsettled given severe pain (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: patients must be able to actively participate in and benefit from the intensive rehabilitation therapy program provided in IRFs
findings.case_fact: experienced severe pain requiring multiple treatments including Norco and patient controlled administration of Dilaudid.
